Lokayukta — Department exercising disciplinary control over departments
x: The State Vigilance Commission advises on vigilance and disciplinary matters. Trap investigations belong to the Anti-Corruption Bureau, while the Lokayukta is the statutory ombudsman.
tq: Start from the sure institutional-function pair and eliminate swapped roles.
sec: Lokayukta vs Vigilance Commission and Anti-Corruption Bureau in AP

s:
Arrange the following in chronological order:
A. First Lokpal Bill introduced
B. Sweden established the first ombudsman
C. Maharashtra established the first Lokayukta
D. First Lokpal appointed in India
x: Sweden’s first ombudsman dates to 1809, the first Lokpal Bill to 1968, Maharashtra’s first Lokayukta to 1971, and India’s first Lokpal appointment to 2019.
tq: Fix the earliest and latest events first, then place the two middle events by year.
sec: Universal angles

s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with the year or place associated with the first institution?
x: Sweden had the first ombudsman in 1809. Odisha enacted the first Lokayukta law in 1970, Maharashtra established the first Lokayukta in 1971, and India appointed its first Lokpal in 2019.
tq: Check whether the option confuses the first law, first office and first office-holder.
sec: Universal angles

s: Who is identified as the present Chairperson of the Lokpal from 2024?
x: A.M. Khanwilkar is identified as the present Chairperson of the Lokpal from 2024.
tq: Use the year marker to distinguish the current Chairperson from the first Lokpal.
sec: Universal angles

s: Which one of the following statements regarding the history of Lokayukta institutions is correct?
o: Maharashtra enacted the first Lokayukta law in 1970, while Odisha established the first Lokayukta in 1971.
Odisha enacted the first Lokayukta law in 1970, while Maharashtra established the first Lokayukta in 1971.
Sweden enacted the first Lokayukta law in 1970, followed by Maharashtra in 1971.
Andhra Pradesh established the first Lokayukta in India in 1970.
x: Odisha had the first Lokayukta law in 1970, whereas Maharashtra was the first State to establish a Lokayukta, in 1971.
tq: Discriminate between the first law and the first established office.

s:
Consider the following statements about the institutional status of Lokayukta laws:
1. Lokayukta laws are uniform throughout India.
2. Their powers are often advisory in nature.
3. Dependence on State police is a criticism of the institution.
4. Executive attempts to dilute their powers have been part of the criticism.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Statements 2, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 is false because Lokayukta laws lack uniformity across States.
tq: Test the exception to a broad institutional claim: non-uniformity is a central criticism.
sec: Universal angles

s: Which one of the following criticisms of the Lokpal institution is NOT correct?
o: The delay has been viewed as indicating political reluctance.
There was a five-year delay before the first Lokpal was appointed.
Inquiry and prosecution wings have remained fully staffed since the beginning.
A two-year vacancy occurred after the first Lokpal’s tenure or appointment period.
x: The inquiry and prosecution wings have not remained fully staffed; their continuing staffing problems are among the criticisms. The other statements describe reported concerns regarding delay and vacancy.
tq: Find the absolute reversal of a documented institutional weakness.
sec: Universal angles

s: The Lokpal’s Inquiry Wing was set up under which provision?
o: Section 7 of the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act
Section 17A of the Prevention of Corruption Act
Section 11 of the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act
x: The Lokpal set up its Inquiry Wing under Section 11 of the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act. Section 17A belongs to the Prevention of Corruption Act.
tq: Separate provisions by identifying the statute to which each section belongs.
sec: Universal angles

s: A parliamentary standing committee observed in March 2026 that the Director of Inquiry and inquiry-wing staffing were
o: abolished after the first Lokpal appointment
still in process more than a decade after the Act
x: The parliamentary standing committee noted that the Director of Inquiry and inquiry-wing staffing were still in process more than a decade after the Act.
tq: Use the institutional-status wording precisely; do not replace ‘still in process’ with ‘fully operational’.
sec: Universal angles

s:
Consider the following statements regarding Section 17A of the Prevention of Corruption Act:
1. It concerns prior approval before investigation.
2. Justice K.V. Viswanathan upheld the provision only when approval is based on a binding opinion of the Lokpal or Lokayukta.
3. Justice B.V. Nagarathna held the provision unconstitutional.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All three statements are correct. The split verdict dealt with prior approval under Section 17A, including the binding-opinion qualification and the contrary view that the provision is unconstitutional.
tq: Retain the separate conclusions of the two judges instead of treating a split verdict as unanimous.
sec: Universal angles

s: In the split verdict concerning Section 17A of the Prevention of Corruption Act, Justice K.V. Viswanathan and Justice B.V. Nagarathna respectively held that
o: Section 17A was valid without any approval; the Lokpal had no role
Section 17A was unconstitutional; prior approval was always mandatory
prior approval was valid only with a binding Lokpal/Lokayukta opinion; Section 17A was unconstitutional
both judges held Section 17A fully constitutional without qualification
x: Justice K.V. Viswanathan upheld prior approval only if it was based on a binding opinion of the Lokpal or Lokayukta. Justice B.V. Nagarathna held Section 17A unconstitutional.
tq: Map each judge to the precise holding rather than remembering only that the verdict was divided.
sec: Universal angles

s: Which of the following correctly states the distinction between the Central Vigilance Commission and the Lokpal in relation to the Central Bureau of Investigation?
o: The CVC has superintendence over the CBI generally in Prevention of Corruption Act cases, whereas the Lokpal has it only in cases referred by the Lokpal.
The Lokpal has general superintendence, while the CVC acts only in cases referred by the Lokpal.
The Lokpal has superintendence over the CBI in every Prevention of Corruption Act case.
Neither the CVC nor the Lokpal has any relationship with the CBI.
x: The CVC Act, 2003 gives the CVC superintendence over the CBI in Prevention of Corruption Act cases generally. The Lokpal exercises such a role only in cases referred by it.
tq: Compare the scope words ‘generally’ and ‘only in cases it refers’.

s: The Delhi High Court set aside the Lokpal’s sanction order dated 12 November 2025 in which case?
o: The Section 17A reference concerning Justice Nagarathna
x: The Delhi High Court set aside the Lokpal’s 12 November 2025 sanction order in the Mahua Moitra case. The Supreme Court agreed to clarify the Lokpal’s sanction procedure.

s: Which one of the following developments was associated with the Supreme Court in March 2026?
o: It appointed the first Lokpal of India.
It agreed to clarify the Lokpal’s sanction procedure after the Delhi High Court decision in the Mahua Moitra case.
It transferred all State Lokayukta inquiries to the CVC.
It abolished the Lokpal’s Inquiry Wing under Section 11.
x: Following the Delhi High Court’s decision in the Mahua Moitra case, the Supreme Court agreed to clarify the Lokpal’s sanction procedure in March 2026.
tq: Link the later judicial development to the earlier order and case instead of confusing it with the Section 17A verdict.

s: The annual report of the Andhra Pradesh Lokayukta for 2025 recorded which of the following?
x: The 2025 annual report recorded 3,654 disposals and recovery of ₹15.29 crore.
tq: Keep the count and monetary figure paired; the distractors reverse or alter one figure.

s: Which one of the following proposals has been suggested in debates concerning Lokayukta institutions?
o: Removal of all investigative functions from anti-corruption bodies
Constitutional status for the Lokayukta and a model Lokayukta Act
Replacement of the Lokayukta by the Central Vigilance Commission in every State
x: The criticisms and debates have included a suggestion for constitutional status for the Lokayukta and the adoption of a model Lokayukta Act.
tq: Identify the reform proposal rather than selecting an extreme abolition or replacement option.

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: State Vigilance Commission — Set up from 1964 on the CVC pattern
x: Section 17A belongs to the Prevention of Corruption Act and concerns prior approval before investigation. The Lokpal Inquiry Wing is associated with Section 11 of the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act.

s: A citizen submits a complaint against a public servant and seeks an inquiry followed by recommendations to the Governor. Which institution most directly fits this description?
o: Central Vigilance Commission exercising general superintendence over the CBI
x: The Lokayukta receives citizens’ complaints, conducts inquiries, makes recommendations and reports to the Governor. The ACB investigates criminal corruption offences, while the Vigilance Commission has an advisory role.
